To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) pose classification is a prerequisite to facial expression classification, (2) pose classification accuracy is dependent on facial expression, (3) facial expression recognition is dependent on the pose and the facial expression, (4) facial expression recognition accuracy is higher for frontal view images, (5) facial expressions are more easily recognizable from profile views for some expressions, (6) facial expressions are less recognizable from profile views in some cases, (7) facial expression recognition from profile views is dependent on the

• LBPs and variations of LBPS are effective for facial expression recognition for frontal to profile views and for different facial expressions • The influence of pose varies depending on the facial expression • The influence of orientation and resolution varies depending on the type of feature used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the influence and potential of pose for facial expression recognition, which has not been previously investigated in detail.
the investigation of multi-resolution and multi-scale local binary patterns for multi view facial expression recognition.

investigating the effects of pose on facial expression classification, the use of LBP and its variations for facial expression classification and the construction of pose dependent and pose independent facial expression classifiers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
facial expressions can be recognised from a range of poses.
the best facial expression recognition performance for different poses is obtained by a combination of pose and pose dependent classifiers.
the best performance is achieved for frontal view images for all expressions, followed by left and right profiles for happiness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pose is a significant factor in facial expression recognition.
the best performance is achieved by using a combination of LBP and LTP features.
the best facial expression recognition performance is achieved at frontal view and performance degrades with yaw variations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pose of a face has a significant influence on the facial expression recognition.
the potential of multi-view facial expression classification is limited to yaw variations of 45°.
facial expressions are most discriminative for frontal and side views, with a gradual decline for profile views.
